tooling.message:
docs: apps live at their developer's hosting; Platform upkeep holds what creators never use

## Intent

The architecture still said that Pages is served below lernapps.net, which is not the default for an app. And blocks named "site" looked creator-facing, although they only serve lernapps.net's own websites.

## Key changes

- An app lives at its developer's hosting, by default the GitHub Pages of the developer's own repo; only a repo of the lernapps organisation is served below lernapps.net. The architecture, the decision, the skill, the plan template, llms.txt and the app publish action say so.
- The deployment view has GitHub Pages and any other hosting as nodes of the app's hosting.
- A new top-level block, Platform upkeep, marked as not used by creators, holds the tooling's build and docs, the platform site actions and the Renovate preset.
- The glossary defines a site as one of lernapps.net's own websites, never an app.

tooling.reason: The modelling of GitHub, decided after the hosting commit; the rename after it is a separate change.
tooling.message:
docs(arc42): GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages and Renovate are external systems, not one actor

## Intent

An actor should be a party with intentions. GitHub only acts through its Actions and is also a hosting target, so a single actor GitHub misled.

## Key changes

- The actor GitHub becomes three actors of type system: GitHub Actions (app check, app publish and check CLI), GitHub Pages (app publish) and Renovate (update policy and preset). The architecture tool has no type for external systems.
- The system context calls them external systems, apart from the parties with intentions; the scenario of a rule change ends with Renovate.

tooling.reason: The rename on the creator's path; one change of its own.
tooling.message:
refactor(app): the app's artifact and job are named app, not site

## Intent

On the creator's path a site must never mean an app, but the checked bundle was still uploaded as "site" and the generated job was named "site".

## Key changes

- The app check action uploads the checked bundle as the artifact "app", the app publish action downloads it, and the generated workflow names its job "app".
- The actions for lernapps.net's websites keep "site".
